title: Three steps of the religion
subject: Islamic Studies
source: Written for islamic-studies/y4 lesson 1 (Pupil PDF worksheet: three steps of the religion)
intro: Lesson 1: Bridge: Islam, Iman and Ihsan (the hadith of Jibril). Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: A visitor in white
points: A man with very white clothes
Very black hair, no sign of travel
He sat knee to knee with the Prophet ﷺ

head: He asked about
The answer in short
rows: Belief in Allah, angels, books, messengers, the Last Day, qadar
Worship Allah as if you see Him; He sees you

keywords.def: submitting to Allah through the five pillars
belief in the heart in the six articles
worshipping Allah as though you see Him
the angel who brings Allah's revelation

questions.q: Define Islam, Iman and Ihsan in one line each.
questions.a: Islam: the five pillars. Iman: belief in the six articles. Ihsan: worshipping Allah as if you see Him.

questions.q: Who was the visitor in the hadith?
Give one example of ihsan in prayer.
questions.a: For example: praying slowly and calmly, not rushing.

questions.q: Draw three steps labelled Islam, Iman, Ihsan, with one example for each.
questions.a: Islam: praying five times. Iman: believing in angels. Ihsan: praying with full focus.

questions.q: Extend: how did Jibril show good manners of learning?
questions.a: He sat close, asked clearly and listened.

questions.q: Stretch: why is ihsan the highest level?
questions.a: It needs Islam and iman, and doing them with the best effort and sincerity.

options: Worshipping Allah as if you see Him
questions.a: A) Worshipping Allah as if you see Him. Fasting is a pillar of Islam and angels are part of iman. Ihsan is the highest level: excellence.

questions.q: Believing in the six articles is called ...
Think again: how does ihsan change the way we work?
questions.a: We do our best because Allah always sees us.
